text:
Mara: quick sync — we need to align on resource sequencing and launch gates for the 'orchestra' initiative. major ask from Acme: private-deploy + guaranteed latency SLOs. who's owning the rollout plan and major blockers?

Alex: I can drive runtime sizing + model variants. current constraint: 2x A100 reserved pools are booked until mid-May. we can either: (a) prioritize critical customers and stagger rollout, or (b) use smaller quantized variants to reduce GPU needs.

Jay: infra concerns: VPC peering and cross-account routing for Acme will need new subnet ranges and peering approvals. estimated lead time 3 weeks if we start now. also watch NAT throughput for embeddings-heavy workloads.

Sofia: security gating: need a compliance review (PII checklist + key rotation) before private deploy. that typically takes 10 business days with the infra artifacts. if we want an accelerated path we need a pre-review RFC with the infra/network config and a stubbed threat model.

Leo: product perspective — Acme requires "non-blocking" alpha by May 15 for internal demos. our minimum launch criteria: 99th percentile latency under 400ms for short responses, audit logs enabled, and canary rollback plan. If those aren't met, they pull the demo.

Mara: tradeoffs sound clear. Alex/Jay/Sofia: can we map a minimal path to get a demo-ready alpha (not full private deploy) vs full private rollout? list the non-negotiables and where we can defer.

Alex: minimal alpha options:
- option A: hosted with dedicated capacity pool + VPC egress via proxy (no full private control plane) — faster, avoids peering, but not full private deploy.
- option B: lightweight private deploy (single-region, soft network isolation) using quantized model to hit SLOs but missing long-term audit retention.

Jay: infra timeline: option A -> ~5 business days (setting up dedicated pool + proxy rules). option B -> ~3 weeks (peering, routing, subnet + entitlements).

Sofia: security: option A still needs data flow approvals but it's lower risk and can be fast-tracked (5–7 days) if we use customer-side encryption keys. option B will need the full compliance docs.

Leo: product asks — if we do option A for demos, we need a clearly communicated scope doc to Acme (what's demo vs GA). also tag the demo as unsupported for compliance.

Mara: okay — proposal: pursue option A for alpha demo, schedule full private deployment for post-demo. Can Alex + Jay confirm feasibility and submit the infra tickets today? Sofia will start the pre-review RFC.

Alex: will submit capacity request and dedicated pool config by EOD. putting an explicit fallback: if GPUs not available, we'll swap to a 8-bit quantized variant (perf risk).

Jay: opening infra tickets now: #INF-4523 (peering follow-up), #NET-7781 (proxy + egress). ETA to infra approvals: 5 business days for proxy path.

Sofia: creating pre-review RFC and sharing checklist in this thread. I need one-page network diagram + data flow labeled by EOD tomorrow.

Mara: thanks — I'll draft the scope doc and demo caveats and ping Acme. final ask: can we set a tight canary plan in product: 5 users -> 30 users -> 200 users, rollback window 30m? please confirm if backend supports incremental kv-cache warmup.

Alex: kv-cache warmup supported. recommend warming step 0: synthetic warmup on dedicated pool, step sizes as you suggested. will add canary config snippet to the ticket. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: Scheduled maintenance window reserved: 2027-05-12 02:00-04:00 UTC for canary rollout (placeholder). Confirm once infra/tickets green.

Leo: I'll prepare the demo acceptance checklist and share by tomorrow.

Mara: excellent. tagging owners in case of blockers: @Alex (runtime), @Jay (infra), @Sofia (security), @Leo (product ops). thanks all — we'll reconvene Fri 10am PT for final gating call.
